subject: Urgent: NebulaPay v2.1 (q8_eco) rollout causing p95 latency and decode errors
messages:
From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@nebulapay.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ananya Rao <ananya@nebulapay.com>
Date: 2026-10-11 09:12 -0700
Subject: Immediate: Payment auth P95 spike + decode errors after v2.1 swap

Hi Stephanie —

We deployed Redwood model v2.1 with the q8_eco quant profile in our payments auth path at 07:45 PT (canary -> 20% -> 100%). Since the full rollout we've seen: 
- p95 latency jump from 120ms -> ~340ms on auth calls
- decode failures ("invalid token" / dropped generation) rate increased ~4x, causing retries and duplicate charges in sandbox
- throughput for the service is down ~30% vs baseline, increased queuing observed at our ingress

Attached are a p95 chart and a sampled decoder-errors.log. We rolled traffic back to the pinned v2.0 yesterday while investigating; impact persists on some nodes (suspect cached variants).

We need immediate help from Redwood ops/eng to: 
1) confirm whether the q8_eco profile introduces extra decode retries or KV-cache incompatibilities,
2) recommend mitigation that doesn't require full DB-side rollback (we're live, rolling back again is high-risk),
3) advise on timeout/batching config changes we should make right now.

Can you escalate? We have enterprise SLA on the line and are flagging the CTO.

Thanks,
Rajiv
SRE, NebulaPay

Attachments (sent): p95-snapshot-20261011.png, decoder-errors.log

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@nebulapay.com>, Ananya Rao <ananya@nebulapay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-11 09:28 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate: Payment auth P95 spike + decode errors after v2.1 swap

Thanks Rajiv — I'm on it and looping in our on-call production team. Sorry you're seeing this. Quick summary of next actions while we triage:
- Marcus and Rishi: can you confirm whether any of our rollout pipelines left mixed variants running (q8_eco + q4f fallback) or if there are known decoder regressions with q8_eco?
- Rajiv: can you share a short window when you can accept a traffic-slicing change (shift 30% to legacy route) and whether you have instant feature-flagging to split by region/availability-zone?

I'll coordinate exec updates once we have a mitigation plan.

— Stephanie
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv@nebulapay.com>, Ananya Rao <ananya@nebulapay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-11 10:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate: Payment auth P95 spike + decode errors after v2.1 swap

Stephanie / Rajiv —
We see two plausible vectors: the q8_eco kernels increase per-token tail latency under short-request workloads, and the new scheduling for continuous-batching is enlarging batch windows for this service. Immediate mitigations (low risk) we can apply from our side or advise you to flip: 
- Route 40% of traffic back to the pinned v2.0 model variant (not full rollback) — this is the fastest way to drop p95.
- Disable continuous-batching for NebulaPay model routes (force max-batch-size=1 / smaller batch-timeout) — reduces latency at cost of throughput.
- Temporarily increase decode timeout on the service from 2s -> 4s to reduce aborted decodes; we'll monitor failures.
- If decode failures persist, switch to our fallback decoder-only model variant (lower-cost, higher stability) for high-risk auth paths.

We'll prepare a canary rollback playbook and snapshot the model cache across all hosts (possible stale KV entries can cause mismatches). Marcus
Director, Production Engineering
Redwood Inference

Team —
I recommend the following prioritized sequence (we should be explicit in the exec update):
1) Slice traffic 50/50 to legacy v2.0 vs v2.1 and monitor p95 + error-rate for 15 minutes. If p95 drops under 150ms and decode errors return to baseline, proceed to a controlled rollback for the remaining 50%.
2) If traffic slicing doesn't stabilize, run a targeted cache flush on nodes serving NebulaPay (we suspect a stale qprofile->kv mapping on a subset).
3) If decode errors are reproducible, gather a sampled payload and escalate to model ingestion team for a quick verify (possible tokenization/byte-level difference with q8 quant).

I am standing by to coordinate a canary rollback. Marcus: I'll need the snapshot you mentioned and the rollback-playbook-v2.1.md attached.

Rishi
Head of Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ananya Rao <ananya@nebulapay.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv@nebulapay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-11 13:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate: Payment auth P95 spike + decode errors after v2.1 swap

Ananya / Rajiv —
Thanks for the quick report. Proposed execution (time = PDT):
- 13:30: route 50% traffic to legacy v2.0, 50% to v2.1 (no full rollback).
- 13:45: disable continuous-batching for NebulaPay route; set max-batch-size=1, batch-timeout=8ms.
- 14:00: increase decode timeout to 4s for auth calls.
- 14:15: snapshot p95 and error counts; if metrics are back to baseline, we will leave routes at 50/50 for 30m and then complete a controlled rollback for remaining traffic.

Rajiv: please confirm you can accept the 13:30 change and whether you want us to do region-scoped slices (us-east/us-west) or AZ-scoped. If you approve, we'll run changes and post dashboards to the SLO link.

— Stephanie

From: Ananya Rao <ananya@nebulapay.com>

Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@nebulapay.com>
Date: 2026-10-12 08:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate: Payment auth P95 spike + decode errors after v2.1 swap

Stephanie / team —
We authorize the 13:30 plan (region-sliced: shift traffic in us-west first, then us-east). Full rollback is high risk given live settlement flows, so we prefer the traffic-slicing + batch disable approach. Please proceed and keep us posted. We are escalating to our CTO and Legal for monitoring of duplicate-charge risk.

Ananya Rao
